thread:
marta: customer report - streaming response ends mid-json, no finish_reason. Happened twice in last 24h. User says final chunk missing when connection recovers after idle tab.

sam: assigned ticket #INC-4821. do we have any recent deploys to streaming infra? :eyes:

support-bot: Ticket INC-4821 created and linked to customer acct redwood-corp. Attach logs and repro steps.

josh: not that I remember. can you paste the raw stream they captured? need the exact bytes.

marta: pasted below (they captured via browser fetch in tab that went to sleep). note the last event is cut mid-object:  

```sse
data: {"id":"tok_...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"...final sentence cut off"

data: {"id":"tok_...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"\n"},"finish_reason":null}]```

marta: finish_reason is missing entirely in the final chunk — they get nothing after the truncated line.

ivy: interesting. two likely layers: browser abort/idle -> TCP RST from browser/OS -> upstream Fastly/edge may tear connection and client reconnects without resume header, so server never emits final close frame.

sam: customer claims their client does a transparent reconnect and expects resume semantics. are we supposed to support resume for SSE?

ijosh: our SSE model is single-stream ephemeral. we do not currently support 'resume' tokens from client — reconnect opens a fresh request. if the client doesn't finish parsing the last event and tries to reassemble partial JSON they'll get duplication/corruption.

marta: customer insists other providers allowed them to resume, but they also used special resume tokens. they said they only used fetch with keepalive true and let browser re-open on visibility.

ivy: quick repro I ran (chrome): open a fetch SSE tab, let machine sleep or background long enough for network to drop, then reopen. observed that final data chunk often arrives partially, and the browser sometimes concatenates headers/buffer which truncates final JSON. stack trace shows connection closed with FIN but no final "event: done" from our side.

josh: can we search logs for the proxied close events around 199888?? I'll grep for connection: close or upstream reset and correlate with request ids. also check if our runtime emitted finish_reason at end-of-stream before the connection tear.

sam: customer provided curl repro — they used curl with --http1.1 and then ctrl-c midstream then re-ran:

```bash
# initial run
curl -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-medium" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -o out1.txt &
# hit ctrl-c after 7s, then re-run
curl -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-medium" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -o out2.txt
```

sam: out1.txt ends with a partial JSON object (no closing ] or finish_reason) and out2.txt contains the subsequent full stream, but the customer tried to join them and got invalid JSON.

ivy: that's expected — our server doesn't produce a durable resume token. best-effort: we can instruct clients to buffer and attempt JSON recovery client-side, or use a higher-level chunking protocol (create message-level boundaries) so repairs are possible.

marta: customer wants two things: (1) guarantee final finish_reason or (2) guidance to avoid corrupted results when reconnecting.

josh: immediate mitigations: 1) advise use of streaming client that handles partial frames and waits for full event object before parsing (e.g., keep reading until matching braces). 2) add client-side idempotency: send a prompt_id and dedupe server outputs if reprocessing. 3) on our side we can add a short grace period and best-effort flush on connection close to try to emit final token but not sure about feasibility across proxies.

ivy: operational detail: many edges (Fastly/Cloudflare) will cut long-lived HTTP/1.1 streams when backend signals connection issues, and they won't buffer partial body. We could switch to chunked transfer with explicit final marker (e.g., a single-line `event: __end__` JSON) that we guarantee to write before closing, but if the proxy kills the TCP before that marker is written it's no help. The only reliable way is an application-level resume token in the payload so reconnections can request remaining tokens.

sam: action items for support: send customer a short KB explaining: how to safely reconnect, provide curl/JS examples for robust parsing, and recommend adding prompt_id for dedupe. Also ask for capture of raw TCP-level pcap if they're willing (hard ask).

marta: drafted KB snippet: 

```text
- When streaming to browsers, prefer using service worker or background worker to keep connection live.
- On reconnect, do NOT naively concat two stream files. Instead: parse each SSE event as it arrives; buffer partial JSON until matching braces; if unable to recover, request a non-streaming re-run for final completion.
- Consider adding a stable prompt_id in requests; on reconnect, call the non-streaming endpoint with the same prompt_id to reconstruct final output.
```

josh: engineering follow-up: I'll grep logs for the two request ids marta attached and check runtime trace to see if finish_reason emitted. if it's emitted but lost in proxy we'll open a ticket with edge provider.

ivy: long-term ask: evaluate adding resume tokens on the stream protocol. that requires coordination with SDKs and correctness around dedupe. I'll write a short proposal.

marta: customer OK with KB and wants ETA on any infra changes. i'll keep them updated. closing loop later. :thumbsup:
